S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

patient_info.stressor_event: Spouse beginning or ceasing work outside the home
patient_info.stressor: After Coleman’s spouse began working outside the home again, his previously flexible routines around the lab, cycling, woodworking, and home brewing had to adjust to more time alone and less shared structure. Over the following year, he developed a fixed belief that certain ordinary changes in his spouse’s schedule and workplace communications carried a hidden personal meaning, and practical explanations did not substantially alter that belief. Because he remained engaged with teaching, data analysis, hikes, and local chess meet-ups, the issue stayed relatively contained, though it created recurring tension at home. He came to psychiatric care through a couples-therapy referral, agreeing to an individual psychiatric assessment when the therapist noted that the central disagreement had remained unchanged despite repeated evidence and discussion.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I know my wife says the late meetings and little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, but for the past year they’ve lined up too precisely to feel accidental, like there’s a private signal in them meant to tell me something she won’t say directly.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: I still show up for my teaching sections, keep up with data analysis, ride my bike, and meet friends for chess; the main place this causes trouble is when my wife and I get stuck arguing about what her work schedule really means.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: It has mostly affected my marriage, with repeated tense conversations at home and the couples therapist eventually suggesting I get an individual assessment. I have not had major problems at work, with self-care, or keeping my usual routines.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about a year, since my wife started working outside the home again.
